title: Window can't be closed on Wayland: Alt+F4 and the close button do nothing
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
**What happens**

On Wayland the ArtCraft Launcher window can't be closed. Alt+F4 and the title bar's close button both do nothing: the window stays open and keeps working.

**Steps**

1. Start ArtCraft Launcher on a Wayland session with a tray available (KDE Plasma here).
2. Leave "Keep running in the tray when the window is closed" on (the default).
3. Press Alt+F4, or click the close button.

Expected: the window goes away and the launcher stays in the tray.
Actual: nothing changes. The only way out is "Quit ArtCraft Launcher" in the tray menu.

**Cause**

`apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs` cancels the close request and then hides the window:

```rust
ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::CancelClose);
self.hide(ctx); // ViewportCommand::Visible(false)
```

egui-winit turns `Visible(false)` into `window.set_visible(false)`, and winit 0.30.13 does nothing for that call on Wayland (`platform_impl/linux/wayland/window/mod.rs`):

```rust
pub fn set_visible(&self, _visible: bool) {
    // Not possible on Wayland.
}
```

So the close is cancelled and the hide never happens. `Shell.visible` is also set to `false` while the window is still on screen, so the next click on the tray icon "shows" a window that was never hidden.

**System**

- ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.0 (`.deb`), also read against `main` at b642df2
- Ubuntu 26.04.1, KDE Plasma 6.6.6, Wayland, x86_64

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: A failed install deletes the verified download, so retrying downloads from zero
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
**What happens**

When the install step fails after a download has finished and passed its checksum, the launcher deletes the downloaded file. Trying again downloads the whole file from zero.

The install step fails for reasons that have nothing to do with the file: the password prompt is dismissed, another package manager holds the lock, the app is running. These files are 100 MB and more.

**Steps**

1. Install any app on Linux with the `.deb` format.
2. Let the download finish, then dismiss the password prompt.
3. Press Install again.

Expected: the verified file is used again and only the install step runs.
Actual: the download starts over at 0%.

**Cause**

`crates/native/src/install.rs`, at the end of `install()`:

```rust
// The download has served its purpose either way; a failed install starts fresh next time.
let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&file);
```

The file is removed on success and on failure alike.

**Proposal**

- Keep the verified file when the install step fails, and delete it only after a successful install.
- On the next Install, check the kept file against the published SHA-256 again and skip the download when it matches. A file that no longer matches is discarded and fetched again, as today.
- Show that state in the UI: "Retry install" as the main action, with "Download again" in the menu to throw the file away.
- The existing 30-day cleanup of the downloads folder (`http::clean_downloads`) already bounds how long a kept file stays.

**System**

- ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.0 (`.deb`), read against `main` at b642df2
- Ubuntu 26.04.1, KDE Plasma 6.6.6, Wayland, x86_64

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Installing several apps at once: all but the first fail with "error 100"
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
**What happens**

When several apps are installing at once (for example with "Update all"), only the first one installs. It opens the password prompt, and while that prompt is open every other install fails with "the system installer stopped with error 100".

**Steps**

1. On Linux with the `.deb` format, start two or more installs so their downloads run together.
2. Wait until they reach "Installing…". The first one opens the password prompt.
3. Leave the prompt open, or type the password.

Expected: every app installs, with one password prompt.
Actual: the first app installs. The others fail with error 100 and have to be started again, one at a time.

**Cause**

`NativeBackend::start_job` in `crates/native/src/backend.rs` runs each install on its own thread. On Linux each thread ends in `run_as_root` (`crates/native/src/install.rs`), which starts its own `pkexec apt-get install -y …`.

Two things follow:

- Only one process can hold the dpkg lock. A second `apt-get` that can't take it exits with code 100, which the launcher reports as "the system installer stopped with error 100".
- Each `pkexec` call authenticates separately, so even run one after another there would be one password prompt per app.

The same applies to `dnf`, `zypper` and `rpm` installs, and to uninstalls, which go through `run_as_root` too.

**Proposal**

- Run the privileged step of installs one at a time: jobs that reach "Installing…" wait in a queue instead of failing.
- Install the packages that are ready together in one privileged call (`apt-get install a.deb b.deb`), so the password is asked for once.

**System**

- ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.0 (`.deb`), read against `main` at b642df2
- Ubuntu 26.04.1, KDE Plasma 6.6.6, Wayland, x86_64

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: UI tests segfault intermittently when run in parallel
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
**What happens**

The UI tests (`crates/ui-egui/tests/ui.rs`) sometimes end with a segmentation fault when they run in parallel, which is how `cargo test` and `cargo xtask ci` run them. The process exits with signal 11 partway through: in the three crashes below, 8, 5 and 5 of the 11 tests had printed `ok`.

**Numbers**

On `main` at e8c4b3d, running the built test binary directly:

| How | Runs | Crashed |
|---|---|---|
| Default (parallel threads) | 40 | 3 (exit status 139) |
| `--test-threads=1` | 20 | 0 |

```sh
cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-ui-egui --no-run
for i in $(seq 40); do target/debug/deps/ui-<hash> >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "run $i: $?"; done
```

A crashed run prints no panic message and no `test result:` summary.

**Likely cause**

`harness()` builds an `egui_kittest` harness with `.wgpu()` for every test, so each test thread creates and tears down its own wgpu device at the same time as the others. The crash goes away when the tests run one at a time. I have not got a backtrace yet.

**Where I have seen it**

- Locally only: Ubuntu 26.04.1, Mesa 26.0.8, AMD Radeon 890M (RADV), 20 threads.
- Not in this repository's CI so far: the two failed CI runs in the history are the formatting check, not this.

It still costs contributors a failed `cargo xtask ci` roughly one run in ten on hardware like mine.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Footer: the rate-limit notice overlaps the links in a narrow window
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
**What happens**

When GitHub's hourly API limit has been reached, the footer shows "GitHub's hourly limit was reached; full details return in N min". In a narrow window that text runs underneath the Website / GitHub / Discord links and the social icons on the right, and the two are drawn on top of each other.

**Screenshots**

Rendered from `main` at e8c4b3d with the UI test harness (`rate_limited_until` set, window width changed), enlarged 2x.

960 px wide: the notice touches "Website".

![Footer at 960 px](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nael-Nathanael/craft-launcher/e84d44357b75e66223a33c689bce34484f1e4a92/footer/footer-960-2x.png)

720 px wide, the window's minimum width: the notice covers every link and icon.

![Footer at 720 px](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nael-Nathanael/craft-launcher/e84d44357b75e66223a33c689bce34484f1e4a92/footer/footer-720-2x.png)

1180 px wide, for comparison: no overlap.

![Footer at 1180 px](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nael-Nathanael/craft-launcher/e84d44357b75e66223a33c689bce34484f1e4a92/footer/footer-1180-2x.png)

**Where**

`footer()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/views.rs`. The left side adds the "Checked …" label and the rate-limit label one after the other, then a right-to-left layout adds the platform label, the social icons and the links. Neither side truncates or gives way, so once their combined width exceeds the window they overlap.

**Expected**

The notice is shortened or truncated (with the full text on hover), or the links give way, so nothing overlaps at any width down to the 720 px minimum.

title: [Windows] 0.1.2 portable crashes on launch in igvk64.dll (Intel UHD 620 Vulkan driver)
author: hungry-detective
body:
## Summary
`artcraft-launcher-0.1.2-windows-x64-portable\artcraft-launcher.exe` crashes immediately on launch with no window. Faulting module is the Intel Vulkan driver `igvk64.dll`. Same crash affects FilmCraft portable (`filmcraft.exe` 0.4.0 and 0.5.0) on the same machine at the same fault offset.

## Repro
1. Unzip `artcraft-launcher-0.1.2-windows-x64-portable.zip`
2. Double-click `artcraft-launcher.exe` (or run `artcraft-launcher.exe --help` from PowerShell)
3. Nothing opens, process exits with `-1073741819` (`0xC0000005`)

## Environment
- App: ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.2 portable, `artcraft-launcher.exe` FileVersion 0.1.2, size 21434248 bytes
- OS: Windows 11 Pro `10.0.26300` x64-based PC (HP laptop, BIOS Q85 v01.31.00)
- GPU: `Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620`, DriverVersion `31.0.101.2140`
- Faulting driver: `C:\WINDOWS\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\iigd_dch.inf_amd64_65ac4d73bb85cb27\igvk64.dll`, same version `31.0.101.2140`

## Event Viewer (Application Error, ID 1000, repeated)
```
Faulting application name: artcraft-launcher.exe, version: 0.1.2.0, time stamp: 0x6aca2397
Faulting module name: igvk64.dll, version: 31.0.101.2140, time stamp: 0x690b539d
Exception code: 0xc0000005
Fault offset: 0x000000000064ea82
Faulting module path: ...\iigd_dch.inf_amd64_65ac4d73bb85cb27\igvk64.dll
```
Identical offset `0x64ea82` + `0xc0000005` for `filmcraft.exe` 0.4.0/0.5.0 on same PC.

## Workaround verified
Forcing DirectX keeps it running:
```powershell
$env:WGPU_BACKEND="dx12"
.\artcraft-launcher.exe
# stays running (tested 5s+, PID alive), default backend crashes instantly
```
So default backend selection (Vulkan first via wgpu) hits the broken Intel Vulkan driver.

## Suggested fix
- On Windows, prefer `dx12` over `vulkan` by default, or gracefully fall back when Vulkan instance/device creation faults (this old Intel UHD 620 Vulkan driver is still very common).
- Consider catching/reporting backend init failure instead of hard crash, and/or documenting `WGPU_BACKEND=dx1…

title: [macOS] Crashes on launch with OpenCore Legacy Patcher: "invalid value 'metal3.2'" (workaround inside)
author: Davidadragoo
body:
**What happens**
On macOS, the launcher window flashes for a moment and then the app quits immediately.

**System**
- ArtCraft Launcher v0.1.0 (macos-universal.dmg)
- macOS Sequoia 15.7.4, installed with OpenCore Legacy Patcher
- Mac: MacBook Pro 15" mid-2015

**Error (running the binary from Terminal)**
```
ERROR wgpu_core::indirect_validation] indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2' ... note: use 'metal3.1' for 'Metal 3.1' standard"))
ERROR eframe::native::run] Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
ERROR artcraft_launcher] WGPU error: Parent device is lost
```

**Likely cause**
The app picks the Metal shader language version from the macOS version (15 → Metal 3.2). On OpenCore-patched Macs, the legacy GPU drivers only support up to Metal 3.1, so shader compilation fails and the device is lost. Choosing the version based on what the GPU/driver actually supports, or falling back when 3.2 fails, would fix it.

**Workaround**
Launching with the system version compatibility flag works:
```
SYSTEM_VERSION_COMPAT=1 /Applications/ArtCraft\ Launcher.app/Contents/MacOS/*
```
The individual Craft apps may hit the same issue, since they use the same wgpu/eframe stack.

title: Every app shows "Not available here" / "Offline" on some Windows PCs (UnknownIssuer)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
A few users on Discord see every app in the launcher as "Not available here" with an "Offline" button. Reinstalling, restarting and switching wifi doesn't help. Hovering the badge shows:

    Couldn't check for updates: invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer

GitHub is fine and other PCs work, so it's local to those machines.

The launcher builds its trust store once from the Windows root store (rustls-native-certs in `crates/native/src/http.rs`). Windows doesn't ship every root up front. It adds them when something asks it to verify a chain. Chrome and Edge do their own verification, so a PC that only uses them can be missing the root GitHub's certificate needs. Antivirus HTTPS scanning can cause the same error.

Possible fix: let the OS verify the chain (rustls-platform-verifier, which ureq supports through its `platform-verifier` feature). PdfCraft's update check loads certificates the same way and probably has the same problem.

title: macOS installs don't check who signed the app or which version it is
author: s17sh70x2jfl031ag
body:
On macOS, `install_dmg` checks the download's SHA-256 and the app's bundle ID, then installs it. It never checks:

1. **Who signed it.** There's no `codesign` call in the install path (`crates/native/src/install.rs`, `copy_app`), so an unsigned app, or one signed by another developer, installs as long as it matches the release's checksum. Windows already pins the publisher (`Learning Machines LLC` in `detect.rs`). macOS has no equivalent yet.
2. **Which version it is.** `read_bundle` reads the app's version, but it's never compared with the release, so an older build published under a newer tag installs without complaint.

The checksum and the app come from the same release, so these checks only matter if a release is ever wrong or tampered with. That makes them defense in depth rather than a live hole. Self-update goes through the same `install_dmg`, so this covers the launcher too.

**Proposed fix**, small and offline:

- After the copy and before the swap, run `codesign --verify --deep -R '=anchor apple generic and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "DJ6XS33FX8"'` on the staged bundle. It accepts only a valid Developer ID signature from your team. Unlike `spctl`, it needs no network.
- Compare the bundle's version with the release's. A bundle that reports only `CFBundleShortVersionString` matches a pre-release with the same numbers, so `-rc` builds keep working.
- On failure, remove the staged copy and leave the installed one untouched.

I checked the current macOS releases of PhotoCraft 0.6.0, LightCraft 0.5.0, VectorCraft 0.8.0 and ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.3. All are signed by `DJ6XS33FX8`, and all still pass after the `ditto --noextattr` copy.

I have a PR ready with tests: unsigned and ad-hoc-signed bundles are refused, version matching (including pre-releases), and a refused update leaves the old copy alone. Two questions first:

1. Is `DJ6XS33FX8` the team for every Craft App, including ones not released yet?
2. Should a failed check block the install (as in the P…

title: Windows: Update all asks for permission once per app; make it one prompt, then install silently
author: KattKnight
body:
On Windows, **Update all** asks for administrator permission once per app, and each app's Windows Installer window opens in turn. Updating five apps means five UAC prompts and five progress windows, one after another, and the user has to sit through them. A user who updates the whole suite regularly asked for this to be one prompt, after which the updates happen in the background while they get on with something else.

## Why it happens

The Craft app MSIs install per machine (Program Files, HKLM), so each one needs elevation. `install::windows::run_msi` runs `msiexec /i <msi> /passive /norestart` for each app from the unelevated launcher, so Windows asks for permission every time. The `INSTALLER` queue (#6) makes those installs take turns, but each turn is still its own elevation.

## Proposal

One elevated helper per batch, which installs every waiting MSI silently:

1. **Collect the batch.** An MSI job downloads and verifies as now, then waits until no other MSI job is still downloading. Whatever is ready at that point becomes one batch, so **Update all** turns into one batch however long each download takes. A job that's cancelled or paused leaves the batch.
2. **Ask once.** The launcher starts itself elevated, once per batch: `artcraft-launcher.exe --install-msis <results file> <msi> <sha256> …`, through PowerShell's `Start-Process -Verb RunAs`, the same way `self_update.rs` already starts `msiexec`, so no `unsafe` code is needed. The UAC prompt names ArtCraft Launcher. Declining it cancels the batch, as a dismissed prompt does now.
3. **Install silently.** The helper runs `msiexec /i <msi> /qn /norestart` for each file in turn. No Windows Installer windows open, and the launcher shows each app's progress in its own window and tray as now.
4. **Report back.** The helper writes each MSI's exit code to the results file, and each job ends with its own result. One failed app doesn't fail the others.

### The golden rule

AGENTS.md says to *never run an installer wi…

title: [Security] Restrict feed-directed repositories and require checksums before install
author: kaboggs
body:
## Summary

I reviewed ArtCraft Launcher v0.2.0 (`bd1182e75c3e631ce877f7317b54b8243e2b4742`) and found two download-trust behaviors worth tightening. I have no evidence that the current feed or releases are compromised. This report describes conditional supply-chain risk.

### 1. The feed can redirect an app to any GitHub owner

`Feed::repo_for` follows `repo_renames` supplied by the network feed (`crates/core/src/feed.rs:128-138`). `RawRepoRename::into_rename` checks name syntax but does not constrain the new owner to `storytold` (`feed.rs:349-360`). The result is used for GitHub fallback (`crates/native/src/backend.rs:693-695`) and accepted as the prefix for release assets (`feed.rs:166-181`). The same path can affect the launcher's own release lookup.

If the feed were compromised, an attacker could point a Craft app to an attacker-owned GitHub repository and provide matching package metadata and hashes. The current URL-prefix and SHA-256 checks would still pass because both refer to the newly selected repository. Please consider pinning an approved owner/repository list, or verifying a migration independently before following a rename. Also bind each selected asset to the approved release tag.

### 2. An install can proceed when no checksum exists

`install::download` accepts `None` when release metadata and `SHA256SUMS.txt` have no digest (`crates/native/src/install.rs:140-165`). `http::matches_published` then checks only the file length (`crates/native/src/http.rs:393-398`). Self-update uses the same download path (`crates/native/src/self_update.rs:169-173`). A same-length altered package would pass that fallback. The user-visible note is added only after install succeeds (`crates/native/src/backend.rs:485-489`).

Please consider requiring a valid digest before install or self-update and showing an actionable error if it is unavailable. Platform code-signing identity checks would add a separate safeguard. I saw the related macOS signature discussion in #50.

author: mahmagha
body:
### Environment
- **OS**: Windows 10/11 x64
- **App**: ArtCraft Launcher 0.2.0 (`artcraft-launcher.exe`)
- **GPU**: Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620 / Intel HD Graphics 500/600 series (Intel Core 6th?10th Gen)
- **Driver**: Intel Graphics Driver 31.0.101.2135

### Problem Description
After installing the launcher, running `artcraft-launcher.exe` exits silently without displaying a window (exit code 101).

Capturing stderr with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` reveals a wgpu validation panic during `Device::create_render_pipeline`:
```text
[ERROR wgpu::backend::wgpu_core] Shader translation error for stage ShaderStages(VERTEX | FRAGMENT): The parameter is incorrect. (0x80070057)
[ERROR wgpu::backend::wgpu_core] Please report it to https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu
[ERROR wgpu::backend::wgpu_core] Handling wgpu errors as fatal by default

thread 'main' panicked at wgpu-30.0.1\src\backend\wgpu_core.rs:1414:26:
wgpu error: Validation Error

Caused by:
  In Device::create_render_pipeline, label = 'egui_pipeline'
    Internal error in ShaderStages(VERTEX | FRAGMENT) shader: The parameter is incorrect. (0x80070057)
```

### Root Cause
PR #105 introduced `adapter_rank()` to prioritize Direct3D 12 (including WARP) ahead of OpenGL on Windows when `WGPU_BACKEND` is unset, to avoid pre-D3D12 legacy GL drivers (such as Intel HD 4000) that fail `Surface::configure`.

However, on systems with Intel Gen 9/9.5 integrated graphics (HD/UHD 500/600 series, 6th?10th Gen Intel CPUs):
1. A hardware Direct3D 12 adapter is present, so `adapter_rank` selects `Backend::Dx12`.
2. Under D3D12 with wgpu's default FXC compiler, creating `egui_pipeline` fails with `The parameter is incorrect (0x80070057)`, causing an unhandled panic.
3. Their Vulkan driver also crashes inside `igvk64.dll` (access violation `0xC0000005`, as reported in #46).
4. Their OpenGL driver, however, supports OpenGL 4.6 and runs the launcher smoothly with full hardware acceleration (running with `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` works completely).

title: Linux: installing an AppImage writes no desktop entry or icon, and installed.json says files: []
author: Qreepex
body:
## Summary
When the launcher installs an app as an AppImage on Linux, the manifest (`~/.local/share/artcraft-launcher/installed.json`) records `"files": []` and no `.desktop` file or icon is written to `~/.local/share`, so the app never shows up in the desktop's menu or app launcher. Observed for both WordCraft and PhotoCraft.

## Reproduction
- OS: CachyOS (Arch-based, btrfs), launcher `artcraft-launcher-0.2.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage`
1. Install PhotoCraft (0.7.0 AppImage) via the launcher, then WordCraft (0.5.0 AppImage).
2. Check `~/.local/share/applications/` and `~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/`.

## Observed
```json
{
  "apps": {
    "photocraft": { "version": "0.7.0", "kind": "AppImage", "path": "/home/…/Applications/photocraft-0.7.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage", "installed_at": …, "files": [], "needs_root": false },
    "wordcraft":  { "version": "0.5.0", "kind": "AppImage", "path": "/home/…/Applications/wordcraft-0.5.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage",  "installed_at": …, "files": [], "needs_root": false }
  }
}
```
- No `ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop` / `ai.storyteller.wordcraft.desktop` in `~/.local/share/applications` and no icons during install.
- Reproduced on a clean reinstall as well: removing WordCraft's record and AppImage and installing again through the launcher re-creates the record with `"files": []` and still no menu entry.

Since `integrate_into()` returns the paths it writes and the result is stored as `Record.files`, `files: []` is a reliable witness that integration never wrote a single file — not even its own `.desktop` entry, whose write failure at most logs a warning ("couldn't add the menu entry"). title: Updating of Apps require local admin credentials in my opinion unneccesarly
author: MMexicann
body:
Currently, the Craft Apps Launcher requires administrator privileges (UAC elevation) not only when initially installing applications, but also whenever an installed application receives an update.

While requiring administrator privileges for the initial installation is understandable, requiring elevation for every subsequent update creates unnecessary friction, particularly in enterprise environments or on computers where users do not have local administrator privileges.

## Current Behavior

1. A user installs an application through the Craft Apps Launcher.
2. Windows requests administrator privileges during installation.
3. When an update becomes available, the launcher once again requests administrator privileges.
4. This happens with every application update.

For users without administrator privileges, this means an IT administrator must repeatedly intervene and enter their credentials just to keep applications updated.

## Expected Behavior

Ideally, administrator privileges should only be required during the initial installation or when absolutely necessary.

Subsequent application updates should be handled without requiring additional UAC elevation, allowing standard users to keep their applications up to date independently.

## Suggested Improvement

Consider implementing an update mechanism that supports non-administrator updates, such as:

- **Per-user installations:** Allow applications to be installed and updated within user-writable directories without requiring administrator privileges.
- **Dedicated update service:** For system-wide installations, use a secure update service configured during the initial elevated installation, allowing subsequent verified updates to be applied without repeated UAC prompts.

This should preserve Windows security boundaries rather than bypassing UAC protections.

## Why This Matters

This is particularly important for enterprise adoption.

In managed environments, users typically do not have local administrator privil…

title: Feature request: Add Japanese (ja-JP) interface localization
author: ukyovfx
body:
## Feature request

Please consider adding **Japanese (`ja-JP`)** as a supported interface language in ArtCraft Launcher.

The launcher currently supports six languages, but Japanese is not available. A Japanese interface would make app installation, updates, settings, and navigation more accessible to Japanese-speaking users.

## Suggested behavior

- Add Japanese translations for navigation, buttons, settings, dialogs, installation/update states, and error messages.
- Include Japanese in **Settings → Language**.
- Automatically select Japanese when the system or browser locale is `ja-JP` or `ja`.
- Support Japanese fonts so kanji, hiragana, and katakana render correctly.
- Fall back to English for untranslated strings.

A translation catalog such as `ja-JP.tsv`, following the existing localization structure, could be a starting point.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Application: ArtCraft Launcher
- Current issue: Japanese is not available in the language settings.

Thank you for considering Japanese localization!

title: Feature: Organize Start Menu shortcuts into category folders
author: VimiummuimiV
body:
### Description

On Windows the ArtCraft Launcher currently places package shortcuts directly into the root of the Start Menu. This quickly clutters the menu.
It would be better if the launcher itself created and maintained an organized structure, for example:

C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\ArtCraft

├── 2D Graphics
├── 3D Graphics
├── Audio
├── Video
└── ...

Shortcuts for each package would go into the appropriate category subfolder.

### Requested behavior

- On install or update the launcher places the shortcut into the correct ArtCraft category folder.
- If the shortcut already exists in the right place, it is left alone (no duplicate is created).
- Category folders are created automatically when needed.
- Existing shortcuts that the user has already moved into their own custom folders should be detected and left untouched, so the launcher does not create duplicates of shortcuts the user has organized themselves.

### Expected result

The Start Menu stays clean. All ArtCraft tools live under a single `ArtCraft` folder, grouped by category, and updates do not create stray shortcuts in the root.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- ArtCraft Launcher
